minutes.headline: Sewer Commission put off the irrigation meter policy until a meter is chosen, but passed the single meter, connection charge and grease trap rules.
minutes.summary: At the second public hearing the commission reviewed updates to the irrigation meter policy, single meter policy, connection charge policy and grease trap regulations. A resident objected that no meter had been chosen. The irrigation policy was not approved and was tabled, while the other three were moved and approved by voice. The commission also discussed Elizabeth Street infiltration, an Attorney General Open Meeting Law response, and the business manager report.

public_comment.topic: Objected that the irrigation meter policy was proposed without a chosen meter, doubted the $50 fee was based on real cost figures, and noted credits may not cover costs.

public_comment.stated_role: manager of a village (mobile home community)
public_comment.topic: Asked whether the $50 annual fee applies to single meters and whether individual unit meters would be read.
Thanked the board for postponing the decision; asked that the chosen meter have wireless capability and that the water department's meter readers read sewer meters too.

votes.motion: Accept the single meter policy as written
Approve the grease trap regulation changes

budget_items.what_was_said: A charge for an extra reading caused by a faulty meter would be deducted from the next irrigation credit.
An annual fee would cover administration and be deducted from the user's credit. A resident questioned whether it was based on actual cost.
Only a small subset of users have irrigation meters, and reading costs are currently spread across all users.
A charge per gallon for infiltration and inflow and a flat sewer reconnection fee were added to policy.
Annual fees unchanged, depending on compliance and internal or external trap.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission tabled the irrigation meter policy so it can return once a meter has been selected.
The commission passed the single meter policy as written, by voice.
The commission passed the change to the connection charge policy, which adds an infiltration and inflow charge and a sewer reconnection fee.
The grease trap regulation changes were moved, but the minutes record the vote outcome as not audible.
The business manager was asked to get a camera inspection price and ask town counsel about Elizabeth Street infiltration enforcement and cost recovery.

why_it_matters: The connection charge and irrigation policies set what sewer users pay, and the tabled irrigation policy means the fee and credit terms for irrigation meter users are not yet settled.
Infiltration on Elizabeth Street adds flow to the treatment bills that all sewer users share, so who pays for the repair is still an open question.
watch_next: Choosing the irrigation meter is to go on the next meeting agenda, and the irrigation policy would return after that.
The camera inspection price and town counsel's answer on Elizabeth Street are due back to the commission.
